name: Transparent Reality (focus-depth control)
summary: Where the two eyes converge sets depth: looking near or far moves a 3D cursor in depth or switches between a near and a far layer, replacing a scroll wheel in VR.
howItWorks: On an Oculus Rift DK2 fitted with two Pupil Labs eye trackers, the focus depth is the point where the two eye rays come closest. A per-user k-nearest-neighbour calibration (k = 3) recognises two depth layers, which was reliable for distances of about 5–25 m. In the study task the mouse moved a sphere sideways and up and down while focus depth moved it nearer or farther, to touch squares placed at different depths; a near HUD that becomes opaque only when looked at is given as a second application. With 10 participants, focus depth performed slightly better than a scroll wheel for depth, without a significant difference, and was preferred.
